actions.action: Slide plant out of pot and check roots
If roots are rotted, cut them away and repot in chunky aroid mix in a pot with drainage
Check top 5 cm of soil and water thoroughly only when dry, letting it drain
Prune fully brown stems and dead leaf edges
Move plant to bright indirect light away from drafts and heaters
If roots badly rotted, take a node cutting with aerial root and propagate in water or moss
Share a photo of the roots and watering frequency

reason: The answer blames watering/root rot first and mentions poor support, small pot and low light only in passing. Repotting is conditional on finding rot, light is one step among many, and proper staking is never advised. Nothing recommended is likely to harm the plant.
